synopsis: The booklet recommends four or five evidence gates whose pass criteria are demonstrated knowledge—such as model correlation and scenario coverage—not dates reached; legitimate outcomes include proceeding, restricting release, changing course or stopping [f9509, f9510, f12301, f16369]. Initial release should cover a narrow operating domain, with expansion to new sites, machine models, speeds and conditions allowed only as evidence arrives, preventing narrow-domain results from being silently generalised [f379, f723, f756]. Gate criteria should be signed in advance with a named decision-maker, safety specialists should co-own them, and an independent acceptance authority must be able to reject insufficient evidence [f12300, f10361, f1586]. The proposed G0–G4 milestones run from November 2026 to August–September 2027, but an alternative layered roadmap places credibility in February–March and evidence release in May–August, so the example calendars are not identical [f12304, f12305, f12306, f12307, f12308, f9875]. Market-access validation is not the only acceptance hurdle: site-specific requirements form a second gate, South African MOSH requirements include no false interventions at TRL4 and no false interventions or warnings at the laboratory gate, and standards applicability remains unresolved pending specialist confirmation [f2931, f178, f12164, f9786, f9787]. Launch and physical-test savings must remain contingent on accepted safety evidence and specific approved simulation substitutions; inadequate evidence must remain a legitimate programme conclusion rather than being overridden by calendar pressure [f10708, f10753, f10909, f10332].
